thesis: Bio-Techne was flat at $72.65 (from $72.81) on 2.2x volume, pinned just under the $73.00 per-share cash price in Merck KGaA's acquisition, agreed June 25, 2026 (company release; definitive proxy filed). Stockholders approved the merger on Sept 23, the U.S. HSR waiting period expired Sept 18, and the company still expects closing in late 2026 or early 2027 pending remaining non-U.S. approvals. With the price fixed, the remaining upside is a ~0.5% spread. The deal was signed more than 15 trading days ago, and the remaining approvals keep the timing open. The litigation check found no lawsuit or investigation over the deal and no restatement (an advisory vote on merger-related executive pay failed, which is non-binding). Medium; avoid.
invalidation: The merger agreement is terminated or a remaining approval imposes a burdensome condition.
sources: Bio-Techne IR (Merck KGaA agrees to acquire Bio-Techne): https://investors.bio-techne.com/news/detail/535/merck-kgaa-darmstadt-germany-agrees-to-acquire-bio-techne-strengthening-leadership-position-in-fast-growing-life-sciences-markets

thesis: Kymera was flat at $173.77 (from $173.92) on 3.0x volume, holding the gains from its Nov 23 BROADEN2 Phase 2b results (company release, 8-K): once-daily oral KT-621 met all primary and secondary endpoints in 244 atopic dermatitis patients (45% placebo-adjusted mean EASI reduction at the mid dose), with a first Phase 3 planned by mid-2027. Kymera priced an upsized offering of 11,638,000 shares at $150.37 for about $1.75B the same day. This run found no new company disclosure today. The drug is not approved and hasn't been tested head-to-head against Dupixent. The litigation check found 2026 plaintiff-firm fiduciary-duty solicitations with no filed complaint or scheduled step, and no restatement. A confirmed readout paired with a completed $1.75B equity raise carries a dilution risk flag, which makes this low.
invalidation: Phase 3 design or FDA feedback undercuts the Phase 2b result, a safety signal emerges, or the shares close back below the $150.37 offering price.

thesis: Insmed was flat at $170.35 (from $170.15) on 4.0x volume, just under the $175 per-share cash price in Sanofi's agreement to acquire it, announced Nov 24 (8-K and DEFA14A), an equity value of about $41.0B. thesis: Amentum edged up about 0.3% to $24.88 (from $24.80) on 2.4x volume, holding the ~20% gain from its fiscal Q4 2026 release (8-K dated Nov 23): adjusted EPS of $0.71 beat $0.66, backlog rose 2.4% to $48.3B despite about $1.5B of NASA-related contract adjustments, and it authorized its first share buyback of up to $500M. Counter-cases: Q4 revenue fell 8% (the company cites an extra week in the prior-year quarter) and full-year revenue fell 4%; this run's sources say fiscal 2027 revenue is guided about flat, with NASA in-sourcing expected to take about 3% of revenue, up from an earlier 1% estimate; and August-September analyst targets sat at $24-30. The buyback and backlog support the read, but the revenue trend isn't resolved. The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement. Medium.
invalidation: Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance is cut, NASA in-sourcing widens, or the shares close back below the pre-report level (~$20.65).
sources: Simply Wall St (NASA in-sourcing headwind, flat FY27 revenue): https://simplywall.st/narratives/p0h3i9x8-ai-and-nuclear-tailwinds-will-support-modest-progress-with-execution-risks?blueprint=4804096

thesis: BIP Inc. fell about 2.1% to $44.56 (from $45.52) on 2.8x volume in its third session under the BIP symbol after the Nov 19 simplification combined Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and Brookfield Infrastructure Corp; this run found no company news dated today. The volume and the 60-day move reflect the exchange into the new entity rather than a new operating result. The litigation check found the pending ICSID arbitration over Peru's Rutas de Lima toll road and a related New York discovery dispute, with no scheduled ruling found, and no restatement. A structure-driven move makes this low; avoid.

thesis: Urban Outfitters fell about 10.3% to $76.74 (from $85.58) on 5.7x volume after its fiscal Q3 2027 report on Nov 24: record sales up about 9% to roughly $1.67B (slightly below the ~$1.667B estimate by one account) and EPS of $1.54 vs $1.53, with fiscal 2027 sales growth kept at high single digits. But the Q4 outlook disappointed: mid-single-digit total sales growth, roughly flat Anthropologie comparable sales, and about 75bp of gross-margin pressure from fuel surcharges; Morgan Stanley downgraded to Equal-weight and cut its target to $80 from $103. Record results offset by a soft Q4 guide make the evidence mixed. The litigation check found only California Proposition 65 product matters (a 2026 settlement and pending lead-content complaints), and no restatement. Low; avoid.
invalidation: Holiday-quarter sales beat the mid-single-digit guide and Anthropologie comps turn positive.
sources: Investing.com (why Urban Outfitters stock is sliding): https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-urban-outfitters-stock-sliding-today-93CH-5050068

thesis: Synaptics was flat at $116.69 (from $116.77) on 2.2x volume, trading under the $123.00 per-share cash price in its amended onsemi merger agreement of Oct 1, 2026 (revised from a 1.350-share exchange ratio after an unsolicited competing proposal), with fully committed debt financing and no financing condition. The FTC granted early termination of the HSR waiting period on Aug 12, stockholders approved on Nov 17, and closing is expected in mid-2027 pending other regulators. invalidation: A remaining regulator blocks or conditions the deal, or the agreement is terminated.

thesis: HP jumped about 11.4% to $31.12 (from $27.94) on 2.8x volume after its fiscal Q4 2026 release on Nov 24 (8-K): non-GAAP EPS of $0.83 topped its $0.69-0.79 outlook and the ~$0.74 consensus, revenue rose 9.3% to $16.0B vs ~$15.3B expected, AI PCs reached nearly 60% of shipments, and it raised the dividend. Offsetting that, fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.15-3.45 sits slightly below this year's midpoint with a weaker first-quarter forecast, management cited memory and storage cost pressure, and coverage of the after-hours reaction was split before today's rally; interim CEO Bruce Broussard has led since February 2026, when Enrique Lores left for PayPal. A beat paired with a flat-to-lower profit guide makes the evidence mixed. The litigation check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement (only a consumer printer-firmware settlement). Low.
invalidation: Memory-cost pressure widens and the fiscal 2027 guide is cut, or the shares close back below the pre-report level (~$27.94).

thesis: Cogent rose about 9.4% to $36.10 (from $33.01) on 2.6x volume, extending its gain after the FDA approved EKITNA (bezuclastinib) with sunitinib on Nov 24 for adults with advanced GIST previously treated with imatinib, its first approval; in the Phase 3 PEAK trial the combination extended median progression-free survival by 7.3 months vs sunitinib alone. Counter-cases: the label carries a boxed warning for hepatotoxicity, and the next binary catalysts are close (an NDA in non-advanced systemic mastocytosis has a Dec 30, 2026 PDUFA date, and advanced SM is due June 29, 2027); Piper Sandler's view that the boxed warning may not carry over to SM is analyst opinion, not resolution. A confirmed approval with an unresolved near-term PDUFA keeps this medium. This run found no 2026 equity raise and no lawsuit, investigation or restatement.
invalidation: The Dec 30 NonAdvSM decision is negative or carries a restrictive label, the GIST launch stalls, or the shares close back below the pre-approval level (~$28).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22 on the Oct 21 proposal; a third sold at the +8% take-profit tier on Nov 24). ROIV slipped about 0.4% to $42.18 (from $42.34), about 1.2% below its 52-week high of $42.70; this run found no company disclosure dated after the Nov 9 fiscal Q2 release. That release reported $31.0M of LISRAYA (brepocitinib) net product revenue in its first five weeks after the Aug 27 FDA approval in dermatomyositis and a planned 1H calendar 2027 sNDA in non-infectious uveitis; an Investor Day is set for Dec 9. The counter-case named in the prior thesis stays open: the uveitis data are not an approval, the sNDA is months away, and the batoclimab Phase 3 miss shows pipeline risk. The litigation check found Moderna's pending Federal Circuit appeal of the government-contractor defense (it decides up to $1.3B more under the March settlement) with no ruling date found, and no restatement. This stays medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls, FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or the Federal Circuit rules for Moderna and removes the contingent payment.
time_review: 24 trading days held; peak gain reached the +8% first tier (fired Nov 24); exempt, the take-profit tiers and the trailing/breakeven stops manage it
